facts.fact: Adding Error Bars to Evals (Evan Miller, Anthropic, arXiv:2411.00640), 45 min: CLT confidence intervals, clustered standard errors, paired tests, power analysis. Read first.
facts.where: rd-se (framework), every section; t-more first paper, 45 min, 'Read first'

facts.fact: statsforevals.com (~30 min): companion resources adapting that framework to small (20-100 item) developer evals
facts.where: rd-test (Wilcoxon row), rd-mult, rd-report tools table; t-more, 30 min
facts.correction: Described from the site itself (fetched 2026-10-04): Ian Arawjo's living guide and the evalstats library, updated August 2026, recommending defaults by simulation (Wilson, Bonett-Price, Wilcoxon, Sidak, Romano-Wolf). It is not a Miller companion and does not restrict itself to 20-100 items; the old characterisation is replaced, not repeated.

facts.fact: The central failing of eval practice is reporting point deltas without noise quantification
facts.where: rd-one lead; rd-report with Bean et al. (16.0% of 445 benchmark papers used uncertainty estimates or tests)

facts.fact: Question-level variance: eval score = mean over items; SEM = s/sqrt(n)
facts.where: rd-se formula (Miller Eq. 1 and 2)

facts.fact: n=100 binary items at p around 0.7: SEM about 4.6 points; a 2-point regression on 100 items is noise
facts.where: rd-se ('4.6 points on 100 items'), recompute.json old.sem100 = 4.58

facts.fact: n=1000: 1.4 points
facts.where: rd-se, recompute.json old.sem1000 = 1.45

facts.fact: Rule of thumb: detectable effect at 95%/80% power is roughly 2.8*sqrt(2p(1-p)/n); invert for n
facts.where: rd-power formula (Miller Eq. 9/10 with z sum 2.80); t-size binary mode

facts.fact: Detecting a 2-point drop near p=0.7 needs roughly n=3500 paired-free; far fewer paired
facts.where: rd-power correction box; t-size preset 'Old rule'
facts.correction: The stated rule gives 8,232 (8,242 with exact quantiles); no variant gives 3,500 (one-sided about 6,500; without the factor 2 about 4,100). At 3,500 items the unpaired MDE is about 3.1 points. 'Far fewer paired': about 1,955 at 10% disagreement (kept).

facts.fact: Paired tests: compare models on the same items, test per-item differences (paired t-test / McNemar for binary); item difficulty is shared so pairing removes most variance
facts.where: rd-pair (formula, animation), rd-test (table)

facts.fact: typical correlations cut required n by 3-10x
facts.where: rd-pair correction box
facts.correction: Unsourced, not in Miller: marked unconfirmed. Factor is 1/(1-r); Anthropic's 0.3-0.7 range for frontier models gives 1.4-3.3x; measured here on RACE-H and MT-Bench (filled live, checked by recompute).

facts.fact: Pairing is the single highest-value practice for regression gates
facts.where: rd-pair closing paragraph ('Pairing is the cheapest precision there is'), rd-power

facts.fact: Sampling variance of generation: nondeterministic decoding rescoring differs; estimate by K resamples per item; variance decomposition between-item + within-item/K
facts.where: rd-var formula and real RACE-H chart; rd-pass MathArena widget

facts.fact: For small golden sets, K=3-5 resamples materially tightens CIs
facts.where: rd-var (Miller: K=2 cuts variance by a third, K=4 by half, limit 2/3; real K curve on RACE-H); rd-one
facts.note: Kept with Miller's exact factors; how much K helps depends on the within-item share, measured here per model (RACE-H, MathArena).

facts.fact: Clustered errors: items from shared sources/templates are not independent; use clustered SEs or overstate significance
facts.where: rd-clu (formula, Miller Table 4, measured ratios, Inspect cluster option)

facts.fact: Multiple comparisons: gating 20 slices at p<0.05 fires falsely all the time; stricter per-slice alpha or hierarchical gating (aggregate first, slices as diagnostics)
facts.where: rd-mult (64%, calculator, Bonferroni/Holm/Sidak/BH, hierarchical gating)

facts.fact: Small-set reality: a 50-item gate can only detect large regressions; be explicit about each gate's minimum detectable effect
facts.where: rd-power ('write each gate's minimum detectable effect next to its threshold'); t-size MDE outputs; rd-mist 'Sizing an eval after running it'

facts.fact: Escalate borderline gate results to more samples or human review rather than re-running until green
facts.where: rd-mult last bullet; rd-mist 'Re-running until green'

facts.fact: Champion passes 78% of a 300-item golden set; care about regressions of 5+ points
facts.where: rd-power correction box; t-size preset

facts.fact: Unpaired: SE of the difference sqrt(2*0.78*0.22/300) = 3.4 points; 5-point drop is only 1.5 SE
facts.where: rd-power correction box (kept, checked: 3.38, 1.48)

facts.fact: Unpaired needs roughly n = 16*0.17/0.05^2 = 1100
facts.where: rd-power correction box and t-size preset (kept, checked: 1,088; 16 rounds 2*2.8^2)

facts.fact: Paired, ~15% disagreement (typical same-tier swap): effective n ~45 discordant items; a 5-point true regression detected with high power at n=300
facts.where: rd-power correction box; t-size preset
facts.correction: About 61% power (normal approximation, z = 15/sqrt(45) = 2.24), lower with the exact McNemar test (filled live); 80% needs about 470 (normal) or more with the exact test. '15% typical for a same-tier swap' unsourced: marked unconfirmed, measured disagreement shown for the RACE-H pair.

facts.fact: Pairing turned an underpowered gate into a working one at zero extra labelling cost
facts.where: rd-power correction box ('turns a hopeless gate into a borderline one at no labelling cost')
facts.correction: Softened to match the corrected power.

facts.fact: Add K=3 generations per item for both models if decoding is nondeterministic; report the delta CI from the paired bootstrap over items
facts.where: rd-var, rd-pass (K samples); rd-test (paired bootstrap, items and clusters); t-lab

facts.fact: State each gate's MDE next to its threshold; get sensitivity from pairing and resampling before buying it with more labels
facts.where: rd-power (bold rule)

facts.fact: Arithmetic that checks out: 4.58, 1.45, 3.38, 1.48 SE, 1,088
facts.where: recompute.json old.*

facts.fact: MT-Bench released GPT-4 grades: aggregate gate at 0.25-point tolerance passes 626 of 1,122 ordered swaps; 67 fail at least one slice
facts.where: rd-mult hierarchical gating bullet, linked to the production page's Gate designer

facts.fact: 70% on 200 items: SE 3.2; unpaired difference 4.6; 95% interval -11 to +7 on a 2-point drop
facts.where: rd-one, rd-se, rd-pair; t-size preset 'Parent topic' (residual 0)

facts.fact: Paired at 10% disagreement: interval roughly halves (±9.0 unpaired, ±4.4 paired)
facts.where: rd-one, rd-pair, t-size preset

facts.fact: Items to see 2 points: 8,242 unpaired, 1,955 paired at 10% disagreement
facts.where: rd-one, rd-power correction, t-size preset

facts.fact: Pair the comparison (McNemar); only discordant items carry information
facts.where: rd-pair formula dl, rd-test McNemar row

facts.fact: Resample when decoding is random, K = 3 to 5
facts.where: rd-var, rd-pass

facts.fact: Items from one template or document are not independent: clustered SEs; 20 slices at p<0.05 trip one by chance 64% of the time
facts.where: rd-clu, rd-mult

facts.fact: State each gate's MDE: a 200-item gate detects about 6 points paired, 13 unpaired
facts.where: rd-power, t-size preset
